kanzAlMahalliRecord.statement: The record assigns the residue to sons, fixed shares to daughters without sons, and a two-to-one male:female division when sons and daughters coexist.

khulasaRecord.locator: references/source-notes/khulasa/khulasa-full.pdf; printed pages 270 and 277–278; fixed-share summary, residuary order, and worked combinations.
khulasaRecord.statement: The fixed-share summary and distribution section confirm the daughter fractions, sons as residuaries, and two-to-one weighting for mixed direct children.

supportingSourceStatus: No project-local Fath al-Mu‘in locator was available, so none is asserted.
ruleSummary: Direct children use daughter fixed shares only without a son; otherwise sons take the residue, with mixed sons and daughters weighted two-to-one.
conditions: A single daughter receives one half only when no son is present.
Two or more daughters collectively receive two thirds only when no son is present.
One or more sons without daughters receive the residue after prior fixed shares.
When sons and daughters coexist, the residue is divided by weights of two for each son and one for each daughter.
exclusions: The daughter fixed-share atoms do not apply when a son is present.
The two-to-one rule applies to the residual pool, not independently to the gross estate when other fixed-share heirs coexist.
Son's descendants and deeper generations are outside these direct-child atoms.
blockingAndPriorityInteractions: Apply eligible spouse and parent fixed shares before the direct-child residual pool.
Presence of a son converts direct daughters from fixed-share status to residuary participation.
A son has priority over remoter residuaries.

sourceAgreement.detail: Both sources agree on all four direct-child branches and on the male:female weight of two-to-one.

atomicCandidateAssessment.rationale: The fixed-share and residuary branches are mutually exclusive and require four separate candidate atoms.

admissionBlockers: Exact source-derived fixtures and a separate calculation-readiness admission remain required.
